title: Duo-euthanasia: When your parents choose to die

body: Bas had planned a scenic route to the hospice, taking in Friesland's meadows and canals."I still remember the whole trip," he says. His mum was in the back seat and his dad sat beside him. At first, they talked. Els seemed resolute about their decision to opt for euthanasia."My mum was convinced, certain about doing it," Bas says. "But my dad was a little bit emotional."Jan asked his son if they were doing the right thing. Bas was thrown - he thought it would be his mum who might have doubts."My mum had always really enjoyed life," he says. "I remember she told me, 'I'd love to be 80 or maybe even 90 years old.'"But his father had been talking about euthanasia for more than a decade because of all the years of pain.In the car, Bas reassured his dad. Once Jan calmed down, they drove without speaking, listened to music and watched the scenery go by.Bas found a parking space."My dad said goodbye to my car - he liked my car, and he said, 'Good job', and 'thank you'."And then we walked inside," Bas says. "Imagine doing that - being in their shoes, taking that trip and that walk. It's so unreal."For the next two hours, the couple's family and friends came and went. They reminisced, and listened to music. At one point, it crossed Bas' mind to call a halt to the proceedings."I had a feeling - 'OK, let's leave… Let's step into the car and drive away,'" he says. "But I didn't want to bring anything up that would make them feel uncertain - I had supported the whole [euthanasia] process."Better to keep everybody calm, and take the moment to say goodbye."Where to get help- The Samaritans, external- Befrienders Worldwide, external- NHS Help for suicidal thoughts, external- BBC Action LineJust before 10:30am, doctors arrived to inject Jan and Els with the lethal medication that would kill them. The couple lay on hospital beds side by side. And in those final moments, before they lost consciousness, Bas witnessed his parents' closeness."I've seen them maybe three or four times in all my life walking hand in hand," he says. "But now they were laying there, hand in hand. And that gave me a really good feeling - they're really doing this together."Bas describes that first half hour after his parents stopped breathing as "a factual thing" - they weren't alive anymore."Then you realise what the situation is - that's an unimaginable feeling."In the hospice, sorrow hit Bas. He began to experience a profound loneliness."Grieving is a very, very deep thing to go through," he says, "and I don't have brothers and sisters - I really felt alone."If we've been brought up by two parents, when the first dies, we can share our memories and sadness with the other as part of the process of bereavement. But Jan and Els were both gone."It was like my legs were cut off," remembers Bas.His grief was physical too - he felt sick for four or five weeks. His body hurt."I would not really recommend this to others, and that's maybe a hard conclusion," he says. "It was maybe for them [my parents] the best option, but having lost them both at the same moment was very, very impactful."Among people planning to apply for euthanasia in the Netherlands, especially those with dementia like Els, choosing the right moment to end your life may be complicated.9,958 people in the Netherlands chose death by euthanasia in 2024427 of those who chose death by euthanasia in 2024 had dementia - six had advanced dementia108 people chose death by duo-euthanasia (54 pairs) that yearSource: Regional Euthanasia Review Committees (RTE)As well as demonstrating they are suffering unbearably, they must be assessed by doctors as still having the capacity to decide for themselves they want to die. This can cause immense distress in dementia patients thinking about euthanasia, explains Dr Rozemarijn van Bruchem, a geriatrician and ethicist at the Erasmus Medical Centre in Rotterdam."They think… I have that power right now, but now is too soon. But maybe next month is too late. So how do I decide at what point I need to start this process to see if I meet the criteria, to see if I can get euthanasia? And if I wait too long, might I have missed the window?"Dr van Bruchem says it's because euthanasia is legal in the Netherlands that her patients experience this anxiety. And they know permission for an assisted death in cases of advanced dementia is rare. In countries where euthanasia is prohibited, like the UK, people with dementia may face many challenges, but they rarely have to weigh these life-or-death options - as Els did.In 2024, she told the BBC that she and her husband couldn't wait because there was a chance her Alzheimer's would progress. And Jan was committed to dying with Els. He told the BBC that perhaps he was going too soon, but he had lived his life – his life was completed.Jan and Els were very aware of the burden their end-of-life decisions placed on their son. Bas attended all the meetings his parents had with their separate doctors during the euthanasia process. There were open family discussions. Often, we have regrets when a loved-one dies – especially about what may have been left unspoken. This didn't happen to Bas. Two days before Jan and Els' appointment at the hospice on Monday 3 June he wrote them a letter."It was about eight pages," Bas says. "I went to the campervan late in the evening on Saturday night. I read the whole letter to them. It was about our lives, thanking them for what they'd done."Jan and Els were deeply moved. And just as they rarely displayed affection to each other in public, they hadn't usually been demonstrative with their son either."You feel that they love you, but it's shown by doing stuff, not really saying it, or giving you a hug," says Bas. "My mum did [hug] more when she got dementia, but my dad never did – I never got a hug."That changed in the campervan on that last Saturday night. Jan hugged Bas."He did it after that letter.  It was maybe one of the best moments."Everything was said."

schema.headline: Duo-euthanasia: When your parents choose to die

title: Top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries 'a hard yes' on impeaching Pete Hegseth
description: The top Democrat widely expected to be the next US House of Representatives Speaker has said he is "a hard yes" for impeaching Defence Secretary Pete
body: The top Democrat widely expected to be the next US House of Representatives Speaker has said he is "a hard yes" for impeaching Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. New York congressman Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's programme This Week that Hegseth had "abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran".Outgoing Republican congressman Thomas Massie, a foe of President Donald Trump, has said he plans as early as Monday to introduce a resolution to impeach Hegseth, which could result in his removal from office.The Pentagon told the BBC it had followed the law and that Hegseth would not be deterred by "phony investigations".As the current Democratic minority leader in the House, Jeffries is favourite to become Speaker when his party takes control of Congress in January following their landslide victory in last week's midterm elections. "I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution," Jeffries told ABC on Sunday."Pete Hegseth has got to go," he continued. Kentucky congressman Massie's resolution contains eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, alleging that he made war on Iran without the required congressional authorisation under the War Powers Resolution of 1973.Jeffries has vowed that the newly empowered Democrats will serve as a check and balance on the Trump administration. But he said after the midterms results that House Democrats were not currently focused on impeaching President Trump, who was impeached twice during his first term.Last week, Hegseth released a nearly six-minute video urging Congress to approve the Pentagon's latest military budget request, before the Republican-controlled legislature's final days come to an end. In the clip, he addressed talks of Massie's impeachment effort, referring to the threat as "sham articles". "You see, their policies don't work. So, their obsession with political theatre disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents," Hegseth said. "It's all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn't work against President Trump and it won't work with me." Impeachment is a rare process by which the House of Representatives can vote to find an official guilty of misconduct and the Senate can then vote remove to the person from office.With more midterm races still to be called, Democrats have a 254-seat majority in the House, well beyond the 218 threshold needed to pass articles of impeachment.But they will fall well short of the two-thirds Senate majority required to remove an official from office, and would require Republicans to side with them - a politically high bar.

schema.headline: Top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries 'a hard yes' on impeaching Pete Hegseth

title: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island
description: Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram
body: Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram alongside a highlights reel of her on the programme that it was "time to throw myself into something new"."While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I'll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever," the TV and radio presenter said.Jama's announcement comes hot on the heels of an appearance as a contestant on Celebrity Traitors that won her praise and speculation in the Times, external that she could "get £1m per deal" thanks to her success.Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an "unforgettable time" on the programme."I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I've loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.But she added: "I've always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."Jama landed her biggest presenting role to date as the host of the reality TV show in 2023, taking over from Laura Whitmore.The programme couples contestants together who then complete a range of tasks and keep swapping in the hope of meeting the love of their life.An ITV spokesperson said: "Maya has been a fantastic and much loved host on Love Island - we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success."Love Island is one of the most popular reality TV shows in the UK but the series has polarised viewers, with some arguing the show is misogynistic and raising concerns about the welfare of contestants.Ofcom has previously received tens of thousands of complaints about Love Island including about alleged misogynistic and bullying behaviour by some contestants.The watchdog has previously described the show as "emotionally charged" with "confrontational scenes" that can upset some viewers.Jama first built her profile through radio including a role on Rinse FM, before landing a presenting role on BBC Radio 1 in 2018.She went on to present a string of television programmes, including Channel 4's Stand Up To Cancer and ITV2's Don't Hate the Playaz, before taking over as host of BBC Three's Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star in 2021.The presenter was recently watched by millions in the Celebrity Traitors final, and competed as a traitor alongside actor Richard E Grant, Youtuber King Kenny and comedian James Acaster during the series.One commentator at the time said that, despite not winning the show, she had emerged as a winner of sorts as she was able to portray herself as "less like the presenter of Love Island and more like a genuinely versatile television star".Her Celebrity Traitors appearance came after she made her acting debut in the second series of Guy Ritchie's Netflix drama The Gentlemen alongside Theo James and Kaya Scodelario.Jama had auditioned for the cult Channel 4 series Skins, set in her hometown of Bristol, when she was 15, reaching the final stage for a role in the show that launched the careers of actors Daniel Kaluuya and Dev Patel.She moved to London when she was 16 to pursue a career in the entertainment industry.She began presenting a weekly music video countdown for production company JumpOff TV before joining MTV in 2014 as a presenter on The Wrap Up.Jama became the youngest person to host the MOBO Awards, alongside Marvin Humes, in 2017.

schema.headline: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island

title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
description: Iran has executed three men accused of carrying out armed unrest during January's anti-government protests, according to state media.Hassan Dioband, H
body: Iran has executed three men accused of carrying out armed unrest during January's anti-government protests, according to state media.Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were accused of throwing Molotov cocktails and grenades, using bladed weapons and firearms, and setting fire to public facilities in the city of Karaj, west of Tehran, Iran's state news agency Tasnim, external reported.The executions are the latest in a series linked to the protests, including those of people accused of having ties to Israel and the United States.The number of executions in Iran has increased since US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic began in late February.The protest movement initially sparked in December last year by the high cost of living rapidly evolved into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on 8 and 9 of January.Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths, and blamed the violence on "terrorist acts" orchestrated by the US and Israel.However foreign-based NGOs gave higher figures and the BBC received multiple accounts from Iranians of security forces opening fire on unarmed protesters.Tasnim reported that the three men were executed after the Supreme Court upheld their convictions and found them guilty of "participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups".The damage allegedly included an electricity substation in Karaj which caused power outages in some areas.Dioband was arrested on 11 January after investigations identified him as a suspect in attacks on public property and incitement to violence.Ten others accused of taking part in the unrest under his supervision were later arrested.Reuters news agency reports that they received prison terms of 5 to 10 years.The latest executions in Iran come after the UN human rights chief Volker Türk said he was alarmed by the rise in death penalties.In August, Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests.Iran is thought to be the world's second-most prolific executioner after China. Last year, it put to death at least 2,159 people, according to Amnesty International.The human rights group said that was the highest figure on record since 1981 and included 45 executions of suspected dissidents on national security-related charges.

schema.headline: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests

title: England 45-22 Australia: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso burns bright in win
description: "Plastic energy."That's what Bongi Mbonambi described it as.After scraping past Steve Borthwick's side in the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final, the Sou
body: "Plastic energy."That's what Bongi Mbonambi described it as.After scraping past Steve Borthwick's side in the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final, the South Africa hooker was scathing of England's back-slapping and celebrating of in-game wins.By then, it had already become something of a meme. Back row Ben Earl pumping his fist to celebrate Ireland's crooked line-out throw in a pre-tournament warm-up was a particular source of online mockery.But, while it isn't the diesel grunt that can win matches on its own, "plastic energy" is still something.It is the body language that shows mindset and intent, that a team's pilot light is on and burning bright.England had it under Borthwick at the Stade de France three years ago, coming agonisingly close to derailing the Springboks. And they had it in spades in Sunday's 45-22 win against the Wallabies.Earl, inevitably, was one outlet, loudly celebrating a third-minute scrum success.But there were plenty more examples throughout the match. Jamie George bellowing into the stands after the opening score; captain Maro Itoje being surrounded with congratulations after an early charge-down; Henry Slade being embraced after a lung-busting late try-saving tackle on Max Jorgensen.Borthwick needed it all.A report in the Times newspaper earlier in the week had said that a rift between the players and their coach opened in Argentina in July, at the end of the summer's campaign.England's senior players denied it. Nothing more to see, they said, than the transparent honesty of a team where input is valued and improvement is the lodestar.But, they also promised proof on the pitch against Australia. It was a risky gambit.Another misfiring, disjointed, underpowered performance – like that in their most-recent visit to Twickenham, February's 42-21 defeat by Ireland  - would dial up the pressure on Borthwick another notch.Instead, his fired-up players turned up.They did so in the obvious ways. There was gainline physicality, breakdown bravery and crunching physicality.Ben Curry leaping out of the line to land a big hit on fly-half Declan Meredith was satisfyingly old school.But there was more than that. There was a different sort of bravery – the one that dares to chance the arm, throw a final pass and back ability, rather than take a safe option.Full-back George Furbank summed it up. Playing his first Test in nearly two years, his ball-playing smarts were deliciously demonstrated in Jack van Poortvliet's try, hitting a line, flashing a dummy and smuggling an offload to cut the Wallabies to ribbons.Henry Slade and Seb Atkinson pulled strings expertly as well.Immanuel Feyi-Waboso showed the sort of Test match mojo that England must protect at all costs.The Exeter wing, who, like Furbank, has endured a rotten injury run, was electric in the first half.Every time the 23-year-old touched the ball, expectation crackled around the stands. And it was mostly met.In 40 minutes of rugby, Feyi-Waboso made 113m from eight carries, beating seven defenders.All those figures were unmatched by any other England player despite the fact that Feyi-Waboso came off at the break and only played 32 minutes uninjured.The wing's ankle was caught under prop Angus Bell's considerable heft and was cossetted in a protective boot as he watched the remainder of the match from the sidelines.After Feyi-Waboso's absence from the entirety of England's Six Nations campaign, the decision not to remove him immediately and minimise the damage may be one they regret when the prognosis lands.England looked to his pace, power and unpredictability as much as they could, feeding him on a dart off the blindside wing from one promising line-out position.They may be missing it next week against Japan. And potentially beyond.Henry Pollock, with a shock of freshly-peroxided hair, came on and inevitably stole the spotlight, with two tries in a cameo on the wing.But, on the wing, Pollock is a stop-gap, while Feyi-Waboso is the star.His fitness, along with that of Seb Atkinson, will be chief of Borthwick's concerns.A cleaned-up disciplinary display – with seven penalties conceded and only the second time this year they have managed to avoid being shown a card – and breakdown that was quick and clean were major plus points.The bench maintained their dominance with an all-Lions front row of Ellis Genge, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Will Stuart trotting on to turn the screw was a welcome sight."I am really proud," Borthwick told BBC Sport. "These players are a wonderful group. We have had some bumps in the road. We have this age bubble where we have so many players 25 and under who are developing quickly into great Test match players, and we have an older group who are helping to guide them."It is an interesting balance and they are working so well together. They are a pleasure to work with."There are big caveats.Australia were desperately poor. Their players are in the midst of a pay dispute with Rugby Australia, an unwelcome distraction that has gone under the radar given the focus on Borthwick.New Zealand, rejuvenated under new coach Dave Rennie, will offer a far more formidable stress test in a fortnight.But as the team's energy spread to the stands, with the vast majority of the 81,334 won over by the display, Sunday was a victory for England to savour at the end of a difficult week.

schema.headline: England 45-22 Australia: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso burns bright in win

title: Two arrested after police officers hurt in brawl outside Glasgow bare-knuckle fighting event
description: Image source, Gregory HoareImage caption, Officers quickly arrived after young men were seen fighting on the Clyde Arc bridgeUpdated 5 hours agoTwo me
body: Image source, Gregory HoareImage caption, Officers quickly arrived after young men were seen fighting on the Clyde Arc bridgeUpdated 5 hours agoTwo men have been arrested and three police officers injured during a street disturbance outside a bare-knuckle fighting championship in Glasgow. Footage circulating on social media shows a group of men trading punches in the street outside  the Ovo Hydro where the event was held on Saturday evening.More than 20 police vehicles and a police helicopter converged on the area. Three officers were hurt, two of them requiring medical treatment, as they responded to the disorder. Police Scotland said two men, aged 32 and 27, had been arrested and charged with offences including assault, obstructing police and threatening and abusive behaviour. Figure caption, More than 20 police vehicles converged on the area outside Glasgow's Ovo Hydro after violence broke out in nearby streetsThousands of spectators had earlier gathered for the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) event where Sean Weir from Wishaw defeated Leigh Cohoon from Manchester when the referee stopped the fight in the first round. At about 23:10, police said they received reports of a large disturbance in the Congress Road area outside the venue. Image caption, Police Scotland said three officers were injured, two of them requiring medical treatementCh Insp Paul Daley said: "Several officers were assaulted whilst carrying out their duties during disorder following an event at the Hydro in Glasgow on Saturday night."Violence against officers is disgraceful and will not be tolerated. Being assaulted is not part of the job and it's extremely fortunate they were not seriously injured."The two men who have been charged will be reported to prosecutors. Three other men were arrested and issued with recorded police warnings for threatening and abusive behaviour and breach of the peace. Police said inquiries were continuing and that anyone found responsible "will be brought to justice". They have asked anyone with information about the disturbance to contact them., external

schema.headline: Two arrested after police officers hurt in brawl outside Glasgow bare-knuckle fighting event

title: Brent School Street fines at one location exceed £1m
description: A London council has issued more than £1m worth of penalty charge notices (PCNs) to drivers under a School Street scheme in less than two years.Brent
body: A London council has issued more than £1m worth of penalty charge notices (PCNs) to drivers under a School Street scheme in less than two years.Brent Council issued PCNs totalling £1.15m after introducing the scheme outside Manor School in Kensal Rise in November 2024, saying it would improve road safety and the environment.Ward councillor Barbara Want raised concerns about the scheme and claimed that the signs were "too high and not properly visible".Brent Council said the signs in place complied with Department for Transport guidelines, but that it had decided to install extra lower-level signs and gateway features to give more clarity to drivers.In the 21 months the scheme has been in place, the north-west London council has collected £54,799 on average per month, with the scheme only in place during term time.School Streets are being trialled across the borough to enforce road closures during drop-off and pick-up times, policed by CCTV cameras and mobile enforcement teams. Those caught face a PCN of £160, reduced to £80 if paid within 14 days.Previously, it was reported that 70,000 PCNs were issued in 12 months, at a rate of 384 per school day.In July 2025, the two cameras enforcing the scheme outside Manor School raised more than £107,000 in a single month, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.Want said: "For months I have been highlighting the huge volume of PCNs issued to drivers on the Manor School Street. The fact that it has raked in more than £1m in two years should have told them something wasn't right."It is failing children's safety if drivers are still using the road. I fear the scheme is more about revenue generation than improving road safety or air quality."Promise Knight, the council's cabinet member for cleaner streets, transport and public realm, said School Streets existed in the borough "to make the journey to and from school safer for children and families"."The purpose of the scheme is to protect children by reducing congestion and improving air quality."We will continue to review the scheme and make practical improvements where they can help drivers comply."Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external

schema.headline: Brent School Street fines at one location exceed £1m

title: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea: Xabi Alonso tinkers again as Blues lose to Black Cats
description: Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat.Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea's struggles for identi
body: Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat.Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea's struggles for identity continued in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland.It is starting to feel as though the Spaniard is the latest "Tinkerman" at Stamford Bridge, a moniker first associated with Blues boss Claudio Ranieri back in 2002-03.For the first time this season, Chelsea lined up with a three-man midfield - but they were also without a recognised striker for the second match in a row, with Pedro Neto again struggling to lead the line in their loss at the Stadium of Light.By contrast, struggling Sunderland were led by target man Brian Brobbey, who won a 36th-minute penalty after being brought down by Levi Colwill. Enzo le Fee converted the game's only goal from the spot.That decision came moments after Chelsea were denied a penalty when Cole Palmer went down under a challenge from Luke O'Nien, but the video assistant referee ruled that contact had started outside the box.Those two incidents in quick succession meant Alonso and his coaching staff appeared angry on the touchline after the Sunderland goal.However, the Chelsea manager refused to criticise the officials after the game - instead he gave brief answers that changed the subject and were critical towards his players for not carrying out the gameplan properly.Asked whether Brobbey was simply unstoppable, Alonso, 44, replied: "No, he's stoppable. He's stoppable, but we have to do it better than we did today."Out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances. He got the penalty as well."I'm not happy with how we defended that situation. It's something that we could have avoided, something that we had worked on during the week. To concede penalties is not good for us."It left nowhere to hide for Colwill, who was substituted at half-time, with Moises Caicedo filling in at centre-back despite having barely completed a full training session all week and needing careful management of his own fitness issues.Chelsea also created few clear chances, aside from a headed opportunity that £117m signing Morgan Rogers squandered, while Palmer also struggled - days after being left out of the England squad.Before the season started, Alonso said he wanted his Chelsea side to be "unpredictable".Although factors such as injuries are beyond his control, his side have achieved that, but to their own detriment.Only Tottenham (28) have made more more line-up changes than Chelsea (24) in the Premier League this season.In the early part of the campaign, they at least had a settled and exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Rogers and Palmer. It was largely the reason behind the positive start to the season despite failing to keep a clean sheet against top-flight opposition until Alonso's eighth game in charge.With Caicedo injured, they suffered problems in midfield and continued to make changes from match to match, while also experimenting with personnel to fix the defence.However, they largely looked on course to emulate the back-three system Alonso excelled with during his historic German double-winning season at Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24.As Caicedo returned after the international break, however, captain Reece James was injured.Joao Pedro featured in wins against Bournemouth and Everton before sustaining a thigh injury, having already missed Brazil's international matches.Number one goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez broke his jaw in a collision at Everton, while Maxence Lacroix, who had been a near ever-present since joining from Crystal Palace in the summer, is expected to be out until January with a hamstring injury.Defender Jorrel Hato has also suffered a setback in recent weeks.It has left Alonso reacting to events when selecting his starting XI, with the Spaniard saying: "There are situations. Yesterday Josh [Acheampong] said he was not ready to play, so we are short of options and we need to walk through this step."Even when we win, when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting for them to come back because they are important."He admitted his side were missing Joao Pedro, although supporters have also been frustrated that Estevao Willian, who came on at half-time on Sunday, has started only one league match this season.Prior to Sunday's game, Chelsea were averaging just 46% possession. They then dominated the ball at Sunderland (with 68.7% possession) but without creating many significant chances. Meanwhile, only Crystal Palace have conceded more shots on target than Chelsea's 50, while the Blues top the league with 53 shots on target - meaning there have been plenty of chances at both ends during their matches.Alonso can still be pleased with Chelsea having collected five more points than they managed from the equivalent fixtures last season, with the club on course to qualify for the Champions League while sitting fifth in the table.However, that is a low bar after a dismal campaign last season, when Chelsea finished 10th.Going into the November international break, Alonso remains a long way from establishing a style of play, or an identity capable of bringing consistency - although he promised promising in an interview last week that Chelsea would be "different" and "better" by the end of the season.

schema.headline: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea: Xabi Alonso tinkers again as Blues lose to Black Cats

title: White House vows to keep up immigration crackdown after midterms defeat
description: Following Tuesday's results, Vice-President JD Vance had appeared receptive to adjusting their immigration strategy."I'm open to the idea that we shou
body: Following Tuesday's results, Vice-President JD Vance had appeared receptive to adjusting their immigration strategy."I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement - by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labour, for instance," Vance wrote in a lengthy online post reflecting on the results.But the White House's posture appears to have hardened after Trump promoted Stephen Miller on Friday to become his new chief of staff.Miller is widely seen as the architect of the administration's hardline immigration policy during the first and second Trump presidencies. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) sources told CBS that in recent weeks officials have been instructed to aim for about 2,700 arrests of illegal immigrants per day, an increase from an earlier 2,000 daily arrest target.Enforcement sweeps this year spurred anti-ICE demonstrations in cities including Chicago, Minneapolis and Los Angeles. In Minneapolis, two US protesters, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, were fatally shot by immigration agents.

schema.headline: White House vows to keep up immigration crackdown after midterms defeat

title: Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Are 'outstanding' Brighton really Arsenal's biggest title challengers?
description: Few, if any, Brighton supporters could have anticipated just how impressive their side would be during the opening 10 games of the Premier League seas
body: Few, if any, Brighton supporters could have anticipated just how impressive their side would be during the opening 10 games of the Premier League season.A 2-0 victory over Brentford at the Amex Stadium on Sunday afternoon lifted the Seagulls into second place, leaving them to head into the November international break dreaming of what might be possible over the remainder of the campaign.Their sixth win in seven Premier League matches was enough to move them above Manchester City, who suffered a shock 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest less than 24 hours earlier, and underline their position as the closest challengers to leaders Arsenal.With a five-point gap to the Gunners, that is certainly the case for now, although Brighton's influential midfielder Pascal Gross was reluctant to entertain such talk at this stage."No, we are not in a title race," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports after Sunday's success."But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season."You see the Premier League, the margins and you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet."Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum, but we are really pleased to head into the international break like this."But 10 years on from Leicester City's title triumph against all odds, could they really achieve the impossible and win the Premier League?As each week passes, though, it is becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss Brighton's credentials.Having won seven of their opening 10 Premier League matches, including beating Arsenal and Manchester City, the Seagulls have shown quality as well as character.But it is not just their league position that makes for impressive reading. Almost all of the underlying numbers point to a side capable of maintaining their early-season form.Brighton have created the second-highest number of big chances (37) in the division and scored more goals (26) than any other side this term.Much of their attacking threat has been driven by Gross, who rejoined the club from Borussia Dortmund in January, having left in 2024.The German midfielder has spent seven-and-a-half years at the Amex across two spells, either side of his spell back in his homeland, and has re-established himself as Brighton's creative heartbeat this season.Gross has created eight big chances in the Premier League, more than any other player.As well as finding the back of the net against Brentford, he also created at least five chances for his team-mates.It was the 27th time since the start of the 2017-18 season that Gross has created five or more chances in a single match, with only Kevin de Bruyne (48) and Bruno Fernandes (47) having managed more.He admitted earlier this week: "I just keep going. I think I'm fit, I try to prepare as good as I can and try to help the team win games."At the other end of the pitch, only defending champions and current leaders Arsenal have been more impressive than Brighton, who have kept the joint-highest number of clean sheets (seven) and conceded the second-fewest goals (five) in the division."The way they're playing at the moment, Champions League qualification is probably the minimum that you'd expect Brighton to achieve," former Everton midfielder Leon Osman told BBC Sport."They look like a team that has really kicked on over the last 18 months. The football they're playing is outstanding and they are a great team to watch."Can they win the league? I think it would be unexpected if they did, but I expected them to win something this year, whether that is a domestic trophy like the FA Cup or the Conference League."There was another welcome boost for Brighton as Yankuba Minteh made his first Premier League appearance of the season against Brentford.The Gambia forward, who was the subject of an unsuccessful bid from Liverpool during the summer, has been one of their most dangerous attacking players since joining from Newcastle United in 2024.Minteh's return to fitness is expected to be followed closely by that of Kaoru Mitoma, who has been sidelined since May with a hamstring complaint.There is a feeling an opportunity could be seized in the title race this season.Although Arsenal have won nine of their opening 10 matches, they have arguably not been quite as convincing as they were during their title-winning campaign last season and were beaten 3-0 at Brighton in September.Elsewhere, Manchester City fell further behind with a third successive league defeat on Saturday evening at the City Ground.But even if Enzo Maresca's side were to rediscover their form after the international break - and visit Arsenal on 29 November - there remains considerable uncertainty over how their season could unfold following their financial charges.City were found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League financial rules by an independent commission earlier this year, three-and-a-half years after they were first charged by the league. The club have since exercised their right to appeal the verdict and vehemently deny any wrongdoing.However, should they fail in their appeal, City could face a significant points deduction or, in the most extreme scenario, expulsion from the Premier League.Were that to happen, Brighton would, based on the current standings, emerge as Arsenal's most realistic title challengers.In fourth and fifth spot are Liverpool and Chelsea, the only two sides to have beaten Brighton in the league this season. But they appear to be enduring transitional campaigns and are currently a significant way off the pace required to mount a challenge.Osman believed it was the perfect opportunity for Brighton to take advantage as he added: "They have taken time to build this team, letting some of their best players go and redoing the whole thing all over again."Now they just seem to be getting to a point where they'll be keeping their best players. "They are in this great position where it is now time to get the most out of all this ability for their own success, to benefit the club and the fans, rather than just for the financial gain of selling players on for huge profits."

schema.headline: Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Are 'outstanding' Brighton really Arsenal's biggest title challengers?

title: Vinted and eBay could be included in under-16 social media ban, minister says
description: Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.Lisa Nandy said
body: Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe". The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."It came after the Sunday Times reported, external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules"."When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers"."While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted.But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep".He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective."The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year.Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach.In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced. Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective."But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services."

schema.headline: Vinted and eBay could be included in under-16 social media ban, minister says

title: Labubu sales are slumping. Is the craze over?
description: For years, Labubu dolls seemed unstoppable.Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the q
body: For years, Labubu dolls seemed unstoppable.Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the quirky monsters - often paying $15 (£11) or more.Those unable to get the characters they wanted were often prepared to pay much more on the resale market.The hype around the creatures convinced a mega-fan from North Carolina, who goes by the name Ensito, to leave his tech job in 2024 to create Labubu content full-time, travelling as far as Italy and Spain to seek out the latest releases.Ensito has spent more than $50,000 (£37,000) to build his collection of more than 400 Labubus, a figure he tells the BBC he's "embarrassed to say".He even had a row of custom Labubu-like jagged teeth made by a dentist to wear at events.But in recent months, Ensito's once-viral posts about the furry monsters have struggled. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now."Ensito's focus has shifted to other trends like Hello Kitty and squishies.It's a sign that the craze which made parent company Pop Mart worth more than US toy giants Hasbro and Mattel put together may be running out of steam. Analysts believe the Beijing-based brand is struggling to capture excitement beyond a single viral moment.Pop Mart recently reported that global sales in the three months to the end of September had fallen by as much as 50% on the previous year.The drop was particularly steep outside mainland China, with US revenue down by at least 70%.

schema.headline: Labubu sales are slumping. Is the craze over?

title: Ocarina of Time review: Does Nintendo's Zelda remake match its original?
description: But fancy graphics have come at a price - a pivot away from realism into something a bit more cartoonish. Some might even be disappointed by this, giv
body: But fancy graphics have come at a price - a pivot away from realism into something a bit more cartoonish. Some might even be disappointed by this, given the N64 game had quite horrifying elements in places.One was the Skulltula House, a room where people had been morphed into human-spider hybrids."Back when we created the original Ocarina of Time, the means to convey or express ideas was limited compared with what we have now," series producer Eiji Aonuma - who worked on the original game - said."With regard to even the so-called scary elements, we strove to add a touch of the comical."But he told the BBC that enhanced graphics and lighting capabilities unintentionally exaggerated the already-spooky Skulltula House and its potential to strike fear into players."When we carried out the test play, the testers were telling us, 'Oh, this is too scary'," he said. "So of course, in the end product, we've made the necessary adjustments so that we can retain the same balance that we had achieved in the original."At times, the trip down memory lane was captivating. I knew where to go and what to do, thanks to a kind of muscle memory. However, on occasion that took away from the experience - with some tasks achieved too easily and some puzzles too quickly because I recalled their solutions.Some people will love how similar it is, but I have to wonder if Nintendo has played things a bit too safe.I don't think the developers see it that way."Even if the game may look different, we've maintained the essence that the original developers wanted to and hopefully conveyed through the original Ocarina of Time," Fujibayashi said. Don't get me wrong - the game has lots of changes and surprises, and I won't spoil them, but I wish there had been more.Then again, perhaps the best games leave you wanting more.Or as Mike put it: "I loved the original as much as the next person, but I don't think I'll be going back to it."Fans will no doubt wonder whether this is it, or if there will be more Zelda on the horizon. With the franchise's first movie coming next year, there's certainly more to come in the short term.And in the long term, I wondered if with 30 more years of technological advancements, Nintendo might consider remaking the game once again. "I will be long retired," Aonuma said, with a laugh.

schema.headline: Ocarina of Time review: Does Nintendo's Zelda remake match its original?

title: 'Time is up': Nandy warns media industry to take abuse seriously in wake of Brand case
description: Abuse in the media industry is probably still happening as organisations are not doing enough to protect women, the culture secretary has warned in th
body: Abuse in the media industry is probably still happening as organisations are not doing enough to protect women, the culture secretary has warned in the wake of Russell Brand's conviction.Lisa Nandy told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme: "Time is up, it really is time for the media industry to take this seriously."She added that since entering government, "many people" from within the industry had reached out to her "to allege that things have happened to them".Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault after a four-week trial, following allegations from multiple women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.Nandy was asked whether she believed there was still exploitation and abuse within the media industry, following the Brand trial and cancellation of Channel 4 reality show Married at First Sight after the BBC revealed rape allegations. She said: "I do not see that much has changed in terms of the way that institutions in the media industry and across public life, including politics, deal with women who very bravely come forward to allege abuse."Nandy added that there was often no protection and a "very heavy cost" for women who speak up in industries such as media and politics, pointing to power imbalances and short-term contracts some staff members are given."Hand on heart, I can't say to you as the culture secretary that this is not happening today. In fact, if I had to wager, I would say it is," she said. Nandy said many had come forward from within the industry, including from the BBC.But she added that the BBC had been an "exemplar" in signing up to the industry body to protect whistleblowers - the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority - and urged other organisations to follow suit.A BBC spokesperson said the broadcaster "has made a significant commitment to improve its culture, processes and standards"."Last year, following an independent culture review, we set out the behavioural expectations for everyone who works with or for the BBC and we were clear action would be taken if these were not met," the spokesperson added.

schema.headline: 'Time is up': Nandy warns media industry to take abuse seriously in wake of Brand case
